items.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

ctx.x: Tell me what a typical week is like for a musician like yourself in New York.

For me? Watching Jerry Springer. No. Sometimes it’s like that for a musician, you know, watching TV. A good week is getting calls from different people. A good week is hooking up a session with somebody, getting a call to go to Lebanon, getting a call to go to Japan. I haven’t written as much in recent years. I used to write music every day in high school. What’s happened now is that a lot of my old stuff is being recorded now.
